data_presentation.notes: Pull stat is clean and does analytical work, not decoration. All numbers carry citations: 1,198,300 population, 156 complaints, 2,791 + 422 prior recalls, ~13 per 100K. Actionable takeaways are specific: VIN check with recall numbers 21V-835 and 23V-235, the noise-before-failure tell, and the 'file the complaint' ask that ties the remedy to the mechanism (the population estimate runs on complaints).

ethics_reviewer.notes: Counterargument paragraph at full strength: PE is the mildest stage, zero crashes/injuries/fatalities, fore/aft links are adjacent not identical. Limitations explicit in disclaimer too. No moralizing. All hard claims sourced. The 'which of those stories was true' closer is a question, not an accusation.

general_editor.notes: Headline is specific and verifiable: the blame-the-driver claim traces to Reuters 2023, the probe to PE26006. Lede drops the investigation number and population in sentence one. Pull stat (3,213) sets up the batch-vs-scope argument that carries the piece. Structure flows: failure -> prior recalls -> documented company history -> fairness caveat -> arithmetic -> actionable close. Rex voice sustained. One long paragraph (2023 history) could split, but it holds as a single noir paragraph.

legal_accuracy.notes: All claims sourced to NHTSA resume (PE26006), Reuters (2023 special report, July 2026 probe), Senate letter, Autobody News. No defamation risk: the blame-the-driver conduct is documented in Reuters company records and a 2020 Tesla letter to NHTSA. Pre-score fix applied: closing 'called these parts flawed' softened to the documented 'ordered repeated redesigns... and discussed billing suppliers.' The adjacent-not-identical caveat preempts misrepresentation of the component link.

research_rigor.notes: Five sources, four primary (NHTSA ODI resume, two Reuters pieces, Senate letter). Novel contribution: 0.27% population-to-recall math, the China-vs-US recall divergence, batch-vs-scope framing from NHTSA's own 'not related to the production issue' language. Limitations acknowledged (hosted copy of resume; editorial inference in linking component families). Kill test passed: this is not commodity probe news.

social_shareability.notes: Headline is the share: company blames customers, feds probe 1.2M cars. The 0.27% stat is quotable and memorable. The China-2020-recall vs no-US-recall divergence gives a second shareable beat. Will draw both Tesla defenders and critics into argument, which is engagement, not misinformation.

voice_coach.notes: Zero em dashes. Zero banned phrases. The-starters 12.5% (under 15%). Sentence rhythm genuinely varied: 1-word fragment, 4-word fragments, then 36-37 word builds. Rex is distinct: 'Read the federal resume slowly,' 'the car went wherever physics took it,' 'Same family, different defendant.' No AI tells. 554 words, slightly over 500 target but justified for an investigation with a fairness caveat.

decision: SHIP_BLOCKED (1/day rule: #878 published 2026-09-11). All gates pass, 7/7 critics >= 8.5, avg 9.0.
